doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Chicago and New York with Dizzy Gillespie
title: Little Diz and Little Bird, the bus to New York and the Hotel Theresa
summary: He recalls two Chicago kids nicknamed Little Diz and Little Bird, then three of them arriving in New York with $5 and staying at the Hotel Theresa.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I’m telling you. Now, Little Diz, trumpet player.
I think both of those kids died early.
Little Bird. Who were they calling Little Bird?
Jimmy Heath? Or are these just guys out of Chicago who had those names?
He’s out of Chicago. I don’t know if he ever . . .

I don’t know what they did in New York, because we – when we got off the bus – we took the bus from Chicago to New York. When we got off the bus, we had $5 between us. But we stayed in the hotel right behind the theater. Stitt and Daughtry: Was that the Theresa? Hotel Theresa?
We stayed in the Theresa. I guess that’s the name of the hotel.
Yeah, stayed in the Theresa, three of us. It was summertime. The other two guys said, “We found a room, but there’s no windows.” I said, “You got it.”
I slept – it’s summertime, so I slept in the – where the mayor’s house is in Chicago.
I don’t know where that is.
